purpose.primary: Expose the project lineage that preceded and contributed to the development of AACCC and 5Guides.
purpose.secondary: Provide provenance-aware material for inspecting how structural concepts persisted, changed, were formalized, were abandoned, or became teachable.
purpose.principle: Origins are an invitation to inspect the path, not a prerequisite for using the Five Guides.

lineage.interpretation: The arrows represent project development, reuse, reinterpretation, refinement, formalization, and educational transformation.

do_not_infer: Each stage logically proves the next.
Each stage is equivalent to the next.
AACCC existed in its current form inside TFT.
5Guides was predetermined by the earliest project materials.
Later formal verification validates every earlier source claim.

student_entry.reason: A learner should be able to practice AACCC without first adopting or understanding the project frameworks that preceded it.

why_preserve_origins.principle: Preserving lineage makes development inspectable without requiring earlier work to remain unchanged.

origin_authority_boundary.principle: Origins establish project provenance, not automatic authority.
does_not_follow: later reuse validates an earlier claim

revision_boundary.principle: An earlier artifact may remain historically useful even when later work revises, narrows, replaces, or rejects part of it.
revision_boundary.requirement: Important changes should remain traceable when they affect meaning or lineage.

stages.name: TFT
stages.title: Triadic Framework for Everything
stages.role: Early project artifact and triadic structural lens.
stages.ai_boundary: TFT should be inspected as a project-origin artifact rather than treated as established scientific consensus.

stages.name: Triads
stages.role: Recurring structural habit across project materials rather than a separate AI Edition file in this scaffold.
stages.structural_contribution: Represent some problems using three distinguishable related positions.
stages.boundary: A triadic representation is a model choice and does not establish that every underlying system is fundamentally triadic.

stages.name: Theorems
stages.role: Stage where several proposed structural relationships became more explicit and therefore easier to formalize and challenge.
formalization_questions: What does a proposed relationship mean?
Which relationships follow from ordinary set semantics?
What follows from a simplified signed relation?

stages.name: RTT
stages.title: Resonance-Time Theory
stages.role: Later project stage emphasizing state, operators, coherence, regimes, updates, drift, and transitions.
stages.ai_boundary: RTT is especially relevant as project lineage and structural inspiration; 5Guides does not require learners to adopt RTT.

stages.name: AACCC
stages.role: Later synthesis of recurring structural habits into five compact inspection questions.
questions: Can this be understood and inspected?

educational_transformation.description: 5Guides reduces domain-specific project machinery into portable student-facing structural questions.
educational_transformation.principle: A learner should be able to use AACCC without adopting the frameworks that contributed to its development.

framework_to_habit.framework_characteristic: May depend on specialized vocabulary, definitions, or domain structure.
framework_to_habit.habit_characteristic: Can travel into unfamiliar domains with minimal specialized vocabulary.

persistent_habits.principle: Make important structure explicit rather than treating the whole as undivided.
Inspect how components relate rather than merely listing components.
Do not force every difference into agreement.
Preserve enough history to understand how the current state developed.
Retain enough lineage to inspect how claims, models, and definitions developed.

what_changed.description: The student-facing AACCC form deliberately removes much of the project-specific machinery.
examples: Awareness does not require RTT field concepts.
Alignment does not require the Nawderian dimension model.
Clarity does not require Unified Resonance.
Continuity does not require adoption of RTT.
what_changed.principle: The educational tool should remain independently usable.

formalization.role: Define the boundary among source interpretation, formal model, proof, and empirical validation.

formal_verification_boundary.principle: Formal proof validates a theorem inside its formal model; it does not automatically validate the broader origin interpretation.
formal_verification_boundary.warning: A valid proof at the end of the chain does not automatically travel backward and validate every preceding interpretation.

empirical_evidence_boundary.principle: Historical importance and formal consistency are separate from empirical support.
empirical_evidence_boundary.rule: Empirical claims require evidence appropriate to those claims.

semantic_drift.risk: A label may persist while its underlying meaning changes.
semantic_drift.response: Preserve version history or explicit semantic transition when the change matters.

lineage_not_one_to_one.principle: Do not force each origin stage into exactly one AACCC Guide.
lineage_not_one_to_one.reason: The source stages contain overlapping structural concerns and AACCC is better treated as a later synthesis.

conceptual_map.boundary: This conceptual map expresses educational interpretation rather than a formally proven derivation.

awareness.question: What did each source actually state?

alignment.question: Do later concepts actually correspond to earlier ones?

coherence.question: Do the stated relationships hold together?

clarity.question: Can source language, later interpretation, formal model, and empirical claim be distinguished?

continuity.question: What persisted, changed, drifted, disappeared, or became teachable across the lineage?

break_detection.principle: Do not immediately repair a discontinuity in project lineage.
break_detection.rule: Record the break before interpreting it.

formalization_exercise.purpose: Connect project archaeology to explicit formalization boundaries.

valid_responses: This correspondence does not appear to hold.
This term needs a better definition.
The formal model adds assumptions not supplied by the source.
This appears useful as metaphor but is not yet a testable claim.
This structural component is useful even if another claim is rejected.
disagreement.principle: Origins are material for inspection, not doctrine that the learner must defend.

examples: We use this term differently now.
This concept was exploratory and is no longer part of the current structure.
project_self_revision.principle: Preserving earlier artifacts allows revision to remain visible.

files.role: Early triadic structures and operator-oriented origin material.
State, operators, coherence, regimes, drift, and transition.
Formal verification, modeling, provenance, and empirical-validation boundaries.

must: Treat Origins as optional project-lineage material.
Distinguish project ancestry from empirical validation.
Preserve source language separately from later interpretation.
Preserve semantic changes and unresolved gaps.
Distinguish structural resemblance from historical influence.
Permit later project stages to revise earlier material.
Apply AACCC critically to the project's own ancestry.
must_not: present the lineage as a strict proof chain
claim that TFT originally defined AACCC
claim that later formal proofs validate all earlier source claims
infer historical influence from resemblance alone
force one-to-one mappings between origin artifacts and AACCC Guides
erase abandoned or conflicting material to create a cleaner history
require Origins knowledge before allowing a learner to use 5Guides
